title: Why Do Dogs Get The Zoomies? (The Science Behind It)
description:

script: Ever seen your dog suddenly sprint in circles like they've completely lost their mind? Vets call it a FRAP, a Frenetic Random Activity Period. You know it as the zoomies. Here's what's actually happening. Dogs build up a surprising amount of pent-up energy and stress throughout the day, especially when they're crated, on a leash, or just waiting around for you to come home. The zoomies are a release valve. When that energy finally has nowhere else to go, their body dumps it all at once through a short, explosive burst of running. It usually kicks in right after a bath, right after a stressful vet visit, or late in the evening when the whole house finally settles down. That timing isn't random. It's your dog's nervous system resetting itself. The good news? Zoomies are almost always completely normal and even healthy. But if they're happening constantly, several times a day, every single day, that's usually your dog telling you they need more physical exercise or more mental stimulation before that energy has to explode out of them. So next time your dog turns into a furry tornado in your living room, just get out of the way, laugh, and let them run it off.
